title: TV Report: Days After Oct. 7, Ofer Winter Warned Netanyahu Gaza Offensive Would Cost 15,000 Soldiers' Lives
detail: Channel 12 reported Saturday, September 5, 2026 that Brig. Gen. (res.) Ofer Winter — the former Givati Brigade commander who has since launched the 'Amcha Yisrael' party for the October 27 election — warned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the days after the October 7, 2023 attack that the IDF could not effectively carry out a ground offensive in Gaza, and that doing so would result in roughly 15,000 soldiers killed and thousands abducted. The network cited an unnamed former military official who accused Winter of spreading demoralizing assessments that contributed to delaying the offensive. Winter denied the report. The actual toll from the Gaza ground offensive was 473 IDF soldiers killed — far below Winter's reported forecast. The report surfaced as Winter has increasingly framed his political entry around October 7 accountability, arguing the government's three-year failure to establish a commission of inquiry disqualifies the current leadership from continuing unchanged.
confidenceReason: Based on an unsourced Channel 12 report citing an unnamed former military official; Winter denies the account, so the specific 15,000 figure is contested even though his post-Oct-7 warning to Netanyahu is not.

title: Father of Slain Hostage Guy Illouz: State Commission of Inquiry 'Not a Tool to Topple the Government'
detail: Michel Illouz, father of hostage Guy Illouz — who was wounded and kidnapped fleeing the Nova music festival on October 7, 2023 and later died of his wounds in Gaza captivity — addressed the Movement for Quality Government's weekly protest at Tel Aviv's Habima Square on Saturday night, September 5, 2026, before roughly 150 attendees. Illouz said a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 failures 'is not vengeance, not a tool to topple the government,' but rather 'a democratic country's way of saying, a disaster happened here, we need to understand why.' He linked the demand to the broader protest theme of preserving checks and balances, saying Israel 'can't dismantle' the mechanisms that hold government accountable to the law. Protesters and counterprotesters, including right-wing provocateur Mordechai David and supporters, clashed near the square; police intervened.
